rationale: RUST-D24. An actix-web route attribute is an `exports` relationship whose target is a URL. The framework guard listed six verbs while the path extractor listed four, so head/patch were recognised as actix and produced no route, and options/trace/`#[route(..)]` were missing from both — four of the eight routes here were silently dropped. Both sides now read one shared list, and the verb match requires `(` or whitespace after it. The two negative controls exist to make that word-boundary rule falsifiable: `#[getter]` begins with `#[get` as a bare prefix, which is how the old startsWith guard claimed actix, and `#[cfg(feature = "x")]` is an attribute with a string literal that is not a route. Without the controls a prefix-matching extractor would still pass this fixture.
